title: Homily II — Dionysius at the tomb; the robes sent to Blachernae

edition.locus: Migne, PG 96 (Paris, 1860), Homily II on the Dormition, cols. 749-752 (PDF leaves 416-417)

source_text: Παρῆσαν δὲ τότε σὺν τοῖς ἀποστόλοις, ὅ τε τιμιώτατος Τιμόθεος ὁ ἀπόστολος καὶ τῆς Ἐφεσίων πρῶτος ἐπίσκοπος, καὶ Διονύσιος ὁ Ἀρεοπαγίτης, καθὼς αὐτὸς ὁ μέγας Διονύσιος μαρτυρεῖ ἐν τοῖς περὶ τοῦ μακαρίου Ἱεροθέου καὶ αὐτοῦ τότε παρόντος, πρὸς τὸν ῥηθέντα ἀπόστολον Τιμόθεον πονηθεῖσι λόγοις, οὑτωσὶ λέγων· Ἐπεὶ καὶ παρ' αὐτοῖς τοῖς θεολήπτοις ἡμῶν ἱεράρχαις, ἡνίκα καὶ ἡμεῖς, ὡς οἶσθα καὶ αὐτὸς, καὶ πολλοὶ τῶν ἱερῶν ἡμῶν ἀδελφῶν ἐπὶ τὴν θέαν τοῦ ζωαρχικοῦ σώματος συνεληλύθαμεν· παρῆν δὲ καὶ ὁ ἀδελφόθεος Ἰάκωβος, καὶ Πέτρος, ἡ κορυφαία καὶ πρεσβυτάτη τῶν θεολόγων ἀκρότης. Εἶτα ἐδόκει μετὰ τὴν θέαν ὑμνῆσαι τοὺς ἱεράρχας ἅπαντας, ὡς ἕκαστος ἦν ἱκανὸς, τὴν ἀπειροδύναμον ἀγαθότητα τῆς θεαρχικῆς εὐσθενείας. Πάντων ἐκράτει μετὰ τοὺς θεολόγους, ὡς οἶσθα, τῶν ἄλλων ἱερομυστῶν, ὅλος ἐκδημῶν, ὅλος ἐξιστάμενος ἑαυτοῦ, καὶ τὴν πρὸς τὰ ὑμνούμενα κοινωνίαν πάσχων, καὶ πρὸς πάντων, ὧν ἠκούετο, καὶ ἑωρᾶτο, καὶ ἐγινώσκετο, καὶ οὐκ ἐγίνωσκε, θεόληπτος εἶναι καὶ θεῖος ὑμνολόγος κρινόμενος. Καὶ τί ἄν σοι περὶ τῶν ἐκεῖ θεολογηθέντων λέγοιμι; καὶ γὰρ εἰ μὴ καὶ ἑαυτοῦ ἐπιλέλησμαι, πολλάκις οἶδα παρὰ σοῦ καὶ μέρη τινὰ τῶν ἐνθεαστικῶν ἐκείνων ὑμνῳδιῶν ἐπακούσας. Καὶ ταῦτα οἱ βασιλεῖς ἀκούσαντες, ᾔτησαν αὐτὸν τὸν ἀρχιεπίσκοπον Ἰουβενάλιον τὴν ἁγίαν ἐκείνην σορὸν μετὰ τῶν ἐν αὐτῇ τῆς ἐνδόξου καὶ παναγίας Θεοτόκου Μαρίας ἱματίων βεβουλλωμένην ἀσφαλῶς αὐτοῖς ἀποσταλῆναι· καὶ ταύτην ἀποσταλεῖσαν κατέθεντο ἐν τῷ ἐν Βλαχέρναις δομηθέντι σεβασμίῳ οἴκῳ τῆς ἁγίας Θεοτόκου. Καὶ ταῦτα μὲν οὕτως. »
pass_a_gloss: There were present then with the apostles both the most honoured (τιμιώτατος) Timothy the apostle and first bishop of the Ephesians, and Dionysius the Areopagite, as the great Dionysius himself testifies (μαρτυρεῖ) in the words laboured over about the blessed Hierotheus, himself also then present, to the said apostle Timothy, speaking thus: 'Since also among our God-seized (θεόληπτοι) hierarchs (ἱεράρχαι) themselves, when we too, as you yourself know, and many of our holy brothers came together (συνεληλύθαμεν) for the viewing (θέα) of the life-originating body; and present also was the brother of God (ἀδελφόθεος) James, and Peter, the chief (κορυφαία) and most senior (πρεσβυτάτη) summit (ἀκρότης) of the theologians (θεολόγοι). Then it seemed good after the viewing for all the hierarchs to hymn (ὑμνῆσαι), as each was able (ἱκανός), the infinitely-powerful (ἀπειροδύναμον) goodness (ἀγαθότης) of the thearchic (θεαρχική) strength (εὐσθένεια). He prevailed over (ἐκράτει) all, after the theologians, as you know, the other sacred initiates (ἱερομύσται), wholly going abroad (ἐκδημῶν), wholly standing out of himself, and suffering (πάσχων) the communion (κοινωνία) with the things hymned, and by all by whom he was heard and seen and known and [whom] he did not know, being judged (κρινόμενος) to be God-seized and a divine hymnologist (ὑμνολόγος). And what would I tell you about the things theologised (θεολογηθέντα) there? For unless I have forgotten (ἐπιλέλησμαι) even myself, I know I have often heard (ἐπακούσας) from you also some parts of those inspired (ἐνθεαστικαί) hymnodies (ὑμνῳδίαι).' And the sovereigns/emperors (βασιλεῖς), having heard this, asked (ᾔτησαν) the archbishop Juvenal himself that that holy coffin (σορός), with the garments (ἱμάτια) in it of the glorious and all-holy (παναγία) Theotokos Mary, sealed (βεβουλλωμένην) securely, be sent to them; and it having been sent, they deposited (κατέθεντο) it in the venerable house of the holy Theotokos built (δομηθέντι) at Blachernae. And these things [are] thus.
pass_b_english: 'There were present then with the apostles the most honoured Timothy, apostle and first bishop of the Ephesians, and Dionysius the Areopagite, as the great Dionysius himself testifies in the discourses he laboured over, addressed to the apostle Timothy just named, concerning the blessed Hierotheus, who was also present then. He speaks thus: "For even among our God-possessed hierarchs themselves, when, as you yourself know, we and many of our holy brothers had come together to behold the body that was the beginning of life, and James the brother of God was there too, and Peter, the chief and most venerable summit of the theologians, it then seemed good, after the beholding, that all the hierarchs should hymn, each as he was able, the goodness, boundless in power, of the strength of the Godhead. After the theologians, as you know, he surpassed all the other initiates in sacred things, wholly transported, wholly outside himself, undergoing communion with the things he hymned; and all who heard and saw him, both those who knew him and those he did not know, judged him to be possessed by God and a divine singer of hymns. And what should I tell you of the things spoken of God there? For unless I have forgotten even myself, I know that I have often heard from you some parts of those inspired hymns."

When the sovereigns heard this, they asked Archbishop Juvenal himself to send them that holy coffin, securely sealed, with the garments of Mary, the glorious and all-holy Mother of God, that were in it. And when it had been sent, they laid it in the venerable house of the holy Mother of God that had been built at Blachernae. So much for these things.'

I render it as one English sentence, joining it to 'it then seemed good'.

Migne fn59 reports that John of Scythopolis took this as the Virgin's body and that some take it as Christ's (the editor rejects the latter); the English leaves the referent as the Greek does, and the Euthymian narrator plainly reads it of Mary. fn60: εὐσθενείας ('strength') is printed (Colbertine, Germanus, Lipomanus) against ἀσθενείας ('weakness') of the received Dionysius text; the printed reading is followed: 'the strength of the Godhead' (θεαρχικῆς).
'ἀδελφόθεος' rendered 'the brother of God', the liturgical title of James; it rests on Galatians 1:19 ('James, the Lord's brother') but is a title, not a quotation, so it is not cited.

'ὅλος ἐκδημῶν' (wholly away from home, i.e. out of himself in ecstasy) rendered 'wholly transported'.
'οἱ βασιλεῖς' rendered 'the sovereigns' (Marcian and Pulcheria, row '2').

source_notes: Second half of PG section 18 (ιη'), continuing the Euthymian History quotation directly after the existing row '2' (which ends '... καὶ καθολικῆς ἀναστάσεως.' in col. 749). Cols. 749 (leaf 416) to 752 (leaf 417). The words of Dionysius (Ἐπεὶ καὶ παρ' αὐτοῖς ... ἐπακούσας) are italic in the print = Ps.-Dionysius, De divinis nominibus 3.2 (fn61). The closing clause 'αὐτοῖς ἀποσταλῆναι· καὶ ταύτην ἀποσταλεῖσαν κατέθεντο ... οἴκῳ τῆς ἁγίας Θεοτόκου. Καὶ ταῦτα μὲν οὕτως. »' is set as full-width overflow lines across cols. 751-752 and was read from the image. Apparatus: fn59 τοῦ ζωαρχικοῦ σώματος: long editorial note (John of Scythopolis took it to be the Virgin's body; some take it as Christ's, which the editor rejects; on the feast, Nicephorus Callistus Hist. 17.28); fn60 εὐσθενείας: so Colb. Germ. and Lipomanus, not ἀσθενείας (the received Ps.-Dionysius text). The word ἀγαθότητα is divided across cols. 749/752. Allusion: Gal 1:19 (ἀδελφόθεος Ἰάκωβος).
